earlier_rows.conditions: words.py seed 7 fixture, 2,000 messages, 12.2 MB of text, long structured replies, 9 KB prompt, 60 s window, headless Chromium vs --bench-render, 3 interleaved pairs, machine load 6-25. Rust = import incl. JSON parse + first sync + Markdown formatted (open_ms + formatted_after_s of each raw run: 485.5, 527.1, 528.3 ms; first sync alone was 375.5 to 417.1 ms and is not comparable); React = navigation until all messages are in the DOM (that old harness did not check Markdown, so this is if anything a lower bound for React). Third React run did not finish within the 120 s harness limit and is excluded from the range, so the range understates React.
earlier_rows.drivers: React renders every message as DOM and parses all Markdown on the main thread; Rust formats on worker threads.

notes: All values are raw per-pair numbers from the stored files; medians, ranges and ratios are computed by make-runs-json.py. Ratios are floored to one decimal, never rounded up.
ratio_floor_median = floor(median(react)/median(rust)); least/most favourable = min/max of the per-pair ratios (ratio_per_pair_floor lists each pair).
Open times differ between runs because of power profile and machine load; React's open time is more CPU-speed sensitive than Rust's. Show ranges, not single numbers.
CPU totals and single-event stalls are load-sensitive and are not headline figures.
Runs 1 and 2 did not record the power profile; run 1 'plugged in' is unknown. Runs 'run1-200x40' and 'run1-10000' are other workloads of run 1 (5 pairs each).
memory_end_pss uses the Rust RSS as the Rust value (Rust has no PSS measurement).
Earlier rows (fx*, gpu-*) keep their own conditions; see their 'conditions' fields.
